title: Halmos proof: setDesiredAPY two-step gate correctly enforces commit conditions

propertiesProven.claim: When apySetInProgress is false, every call enters the preview branch regardless of bps. No single transaction can commit from a fresh-init state.
When block.number > pendingAPYBlockNumber + 100, every call enters preview (a stale pending cannot silently commit).
When bps differs from pendingAPYBps, every call enters preview.
Commit ⇔ (apySetInProgress ∧ blockNumber ≤ pending+100 ∧ bps == pendingAPYBps). Verified bidirectional.
At block.number == pendingAPYBlockNumber + 100 exactly, commit is allowed (`>` boundary is exclusive on the preview side).
At pending+101 the call falls back to preview.

interpretation: The two-step APY gate is correctly implemented as a state-machine. Profile invariant I9 holds for ALL reachable (apySetInProgress, pendingAPYBlockNumber, pendingAPYBps, bps, blockNumber) tuples. No counterexample exists where a single call could commit an unexpected value, and no off-by-one error at the +100 boundary. This is a positive correctness proof — NOT a vulnerability finding.

crossReference.ECON-004: Front-running of the commit step is a separate concern (the commit is publicly observable in the mempool); the gate itself does what it says.
